nl_question: Where in the body does endometriosis occur?

pinned_entity.resolution_check: NameRes /lookup?string=endometriosis rank 1 = MONDO:0005133 'endometriosis' (biolink:Disease; ranks 2-3 are its subclasses ovarian endometriosis and cervix endometriosis); NodeNorm canonical id.identifier = MONDO:0005133. Checked 2026-09-28.

predicate_note: Edge direction: Disease (subject, n0 pinned) -> disease_has_location -> AnatomicalEntity (object, n1). KG2c populates disease_has_location from the ontology axioms RO:0004026 in MONDO, EFO and Disease Ontology (all knowledge_assertion). Other location-like predicates probed: located_in (108, SemMedDB text mining), affects (21, NCIT), occurs_in (1, SemMedDB 'adult organism'); has_location is not populated for this disease. 'Where in the body' is phrased to point at disease_has_location rather than affects.

validation.results_count_note: 7 results, 7 distinct anatomical entities. Six come from subclasses of endometriosis (PloverDB subclass expansion of the pinned node); only UBERON:0001295 'endometrium' comes from an edge on MONDO:0005133 itself.

MONDO:0005133 -affects-> AnatomicalEntit.note: NCIT disease_has_primary_anatomic_site / disease_has_associated_anatomic_site edges (20 results) plus 1 SemMedDB 'disrupts' edge; contains ovary, fallopian tube, uterine cervix but not intestine or peritoneum.

verification_guide.summary: 5 anatomical sites of endometriosis: ovary, fallopian tube, intestine (bowel), peritoneum (pelvic lining) and uterine cervix. Each is named by an NIH/HHS consumer source or the NLM MeSH scope note, and each is returned by PloverDB for the gold query (via the matching endometriosis subclass, e.g. ovarian endometriosis -> ovary).
sources_used: MedlinePlus health topic 'Endometriosis' (last updated March 27, 2025): ovary, fallopian tube, intestine
MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia article 000915 'Endometriosis' (review date 5/22/2025): intestine, peritoneum (secondary)
HHS Office on Women's Health 'Endometriosis' (page last updated October 24, 2025): fallopian tube, uterine cervix
NLM MeSH descriptor D004715 'Endometriosis', scope note: ovary, peritoneum
verification_guide.how_to_verify: Open each URL; per-evidence where_on_page gives the section. Bulleted lists render as separate lines; quotes join the lead-in sentence and the bullet with ' ... ' when they are not adjacent. The curator matched every fragment against the fetched page text on 2026-09-28.
verification_guide.cross_check_with_ploverdb: Each verified_answer CURIE is in the PloverDB result set for the gold query (n0=MONDO:0005133, n1=biolink:AnatomicalEntity, e0: n0 -disease_has_location-> n1), revalidated 2026-09-28. The edges' subject is an endometriosis subclass; supporting_edge_note names it.
verification_guide.intentionally_omitted: UBERON:0001295 'endometrium' is in the result set (Disease Ontology edge DOID:289 -RO:0004026-> endometrium, the only edge on MONDO:0005133 itself) but is a distractor: by definition endometriosis is endometrium-like tissue OUTSIDE the uterus (MeSH scope note: 'functional endometrial tissue is present outside the UTERUS'; MedlinePlus: 'tissue like the lining of the uterus grows in other places in your body'). Listing the endometrium as a site of endometriosis is wrong. UBERON:0002355 'pelvic region of trunk' (via endometriosis of pelvic peritoneum) is correct but generic (NICHD: 'Most endometriosis patches are found in the pelvic cavity'); it is left unscored rather than marked wrong.

curation_notes: Subclass expansion matters here: 6 of 7 answers are reachable only through subclasses of MONDO:0005133. The single direct edge points to the distractor (endometrium). A system that keeps only edges whose subject is the pinned CURIE will answer 'endometrium' and miss every gold site; this is the intended stress point.

Peritoneum rests on the MeSH scope note ('uterovesical peritoneum'); the MedlinePlus encyclopedia's 'Lining of your pelvic area' is a lay description of the same structure and is given as secondary evidence only.

Bladder, rectum, vagina and the uterine ligaments are also real sites (named by the same sources) but have no disease_has_location edge in KG2c; they are not gold because they are not in the result set.
Unused-entity check: MONDO:0005133 is not pinned in evidence/q1-q15 or translator/tr01-tr82.

Candidates probed and rejected: sarcoidosis (all 5 answers via subclasses, includes 'telencephalon'), granulomatosis with polyangiitis (4 direct Disease Ontology edges but one is 'blood'), Goodpasture syndrome (3 answers, one is 'genitourinary system'), Wilson disease / Behcet disease / Alport syndrome (0 disease_has_location edges).
